purpose: Digest-agreement fixture between AAC's in-repo JCS (agent_action_capsule.canonical) and an independent RFC 8785 implementation (rfc8785 0.1.4, PyPI — the library TRACE's own spec names, trace-v0.2.md §3.2.2), over the cases where RFC 8785 implementations are known to diverge: non-ASCII string values, a non-BMP/supplementary-plane object key (U+1F600, surrogate pair), a high-BMP object key (U+FF3A), and integers at the exact IEEE-754 safe-integer boundary (±(2^53-1)).

positive.description: A format-4 Capsule whose capsule_id preimage exercises every RFC 8785 divergence case. AAC's json_digest() and an independent sha256(rfc8785.dumps(v)) over the identical preimage produce byte-identical output and therefore the same hex digest.

mutant.description: The positive capsule with exactly one nested value changed (extension.trace_digest_agreement_test.😀, three levels deep, from "surrogate-pair key" to "MUTATED nested value"). Both implementations must produce a digest that differs from the positive case's pinned capsule_id — if a canonicalizer instead dropped or flattened the nested object (the replacer-array defect documented in the crosswalk prose), this digest would stay 1f6f40b6... and the mutant would go undetected.

boundary_exceeded.description: The positive capsule's extension.trace_digest_agreement_test.safe_max raised by 1, to 9007199254740992 = 2^53, the first value at which npm's canonicalize 4.0.0 and PyPI's rfc8785 0.1.4 are documented (trace-v0.2.md §3.2.2) to disagree — canonicalize serializes it as a double (colliding with 9007199254740993), rfc8785 refuses it. Neither AAC's json_digest() nor rfc8785.dumps() can produce a digest for this object: both raise before any bytes are emitted, so the case where the two libraries silently disagree cannot arise in material either format actually digests.
